title: browserbase/stagehand — The SDK to extract data and interact with any site on the web. Get started with Claude Code, Codex, Eve, Mastra, and more.

report.summary: Browserbase's Stagehand SDK lets developers build browser agents that observe, act, and extract schema-validated data across TypeScript, Python, and Go.
report.background: Browser automation has long meant brittle code: Playwright and Puppeteer selectors break whenever a site redesigns, and teams maintain scrapers more than they use them. LLM agents promised relief, but first-generation "computer use" approaches were slow, costly, and non-deterministic, routing every click through a model. Browserbase, which sells cloud browsers purpose-built for AI agents, has been assembling infrastructure for this growing "browser agent" category, and Stagehand is its developer-facing layer. Version 4 reframes automation as a hybrid: deterministic Playwright-style control where reliability matters, natural-language primitives where pages are unpredictable. It arrives as the Model Context Protocol standardizes how agents reach external tools, making a hosted browser server as easy to attach as any other integration.
key_points: Stagehand centers on three primitives. observe() returns real DOM selectors so sensitive values like passwords never reach the model; act() executes natural-language instructions and self-heals when a site redesigns its form; extract() returns schema-validated output using Zod in TypeScript, Pydantic in Python, or native Go types.

The SDK ships in TypeScript, Python, and Go with near-identical APIs. The same script can launch a local Chrome instance with persisted cookies in ./browser-data, so repeat runs start already signed in, or point at Browserbase's cloud browsers for scale and verification.

Hosted configuration adds a Model Gateway that picks the cheapest model per action without provider wiring, plus server-side caching where identical calls return from Browserbase with no tokens spent. Browserbase claims roughly 2x faster execution than equivalent Playwright cloud browsers.

A hosted Browserbase MCP server exposes navigate, act, observe, and extract to any MCP client, including Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, via a single HTTP endpoint and API key, requiring no local browser install.

Cloud sessions bundle verified mode, residential proxies, persistent contexts, and session recordings, aimed at teams running long-lived authenticated agents against production sites rather than one-off scrapes.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Stagehand is a signal that browser agents are consolidating around a thin, standardized layer: model-agnostic primitives plus MCP distribution, rather than proprietary end-to-end stacks. For developers, it lowers the cost of building reliable agents by mixing deterministic selectors with LLM fallbacks, and its caching and Model Gateway directly attack the two biggest production complaints, token spend and latency. For regular users, the practical effect is more capable web agents that survive site redesigns and stay logged in, but also more automated traffic hitting sites that never consented to it, keeping bot detection, terms-of-service, and credential-handling questions squarely in focus.
report.tools: Worth watching: Stagehand itself (github.com/browserbase/stagehand), Browserbase's hosted MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex, and Mastra for agent orchestration. Compare with Playwright, Puppeteer, and Steel.dev for raw automation, plus Zod, Pydantic, and instructor for schema-validated extraction. For scraping-specific needs, Firecrawl and Crawl4AI overlap on the fetch-and-markdown side.
